page: Amazon Web Services m5n.4xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, offering 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources consist of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set features include AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI) alongside AES and BMI2, though AMX matrix operations are absent. System memory is provisioned at 64.0 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance does not include integrated local disk storage or physical GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached EBS storage and baseline networking throughput rated at 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the m5n.4xlarge in the middle performance tier for multi-threaded processing while demonstrating lower single-thread execution efficiency. Single-core tests reflect lower relative velocity, recorded at 1,139.0 on Geekbench and 1,285.19 on stress-ng, accompanied by bottom-quartile throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. In contrast, parallel capabilities scale solidly into average performance brackets, yielding a multi-core Geekbench score of 7,036.0, a stress-ng multi-core score of 13,538.85, and a PassMark CPU rating of 14,392.67. Memory subsystem performance aligns with expected DDR4 metrics, delivering 89.11 GB/sec on large block uncached reads and 46.62 GB/sec on uncached writes.

Application-level measurements indicate reliable throughput for general server tasks. Redis SET operations reach 13.19 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measures 11.89 GB/sec. On CPU-based inference workloads, small 135M language models achieve 803.49 tokens per second in prompt processing and 139.47 tokens per second in text generation. However, larger language model demands such as 7B prompt processing drop to 19.41 tokens per second, falling into lower percentiles due to the lack of dedicated acceleration.

Hardware tradeoffs focus primarily on the absence of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage integration that leverages its 16 Gbps bandwidth baseline. From a qualitative resource-density perspective, the m5n.4xlarge delivers a steady balance of CPU cores, memory capacity, and network throughput without paying premiums for specialized accelerators. It is suitably aligned for mid-tier enterprise workloads, including web application clusters, Redis caching layers, containerized microservices, Clang-based software build environments, and relational database nodes that do not rely on local NVMe arrays.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the Nitro System, featuring an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) and 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM. It includes 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, 35 MB of L3 cache, and AVX-512 instruction support, with no onboard local storage or GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show solid middle-tier multi-threaded and memory performance, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,036.0, PassMark CPU score of 14,392.67, and 13.19 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside 11.89 GB/sec static web throughput. Single-core processing trends toward the lower quartile across stress-ng and Geekbench suites. Balancing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio with enhanced networking, this instance fits enterprise application hosting, microservices fleets, CI/CD compilation tasks, caching tiers, and network-bound relational databases using remote storage volumes.
